target_customer: Talent acquisition and recruiting operations teams at tech companies
problem: Coordinating many interviews across teams is manual and slow for recruiters, harming candidate experience. ModernLoop automates scheduling and interview logistics.
product_category: Recruiting operations and interview scheduling software

founders.name: Lydia Han
founders.background_notes: YC page: PM lead at Brex, senior PM at Slack, PM at Facebook and Salesforce. TechCrunch notes her sister was a technical recruiter at Brex.

founders.name: Chris Triolo
founders.background_notes: YC page: about eight years at Facebook, the last two as engineering manager; built Facebook's first donation product.

competitors.name: GoodTime
competitors.what: Interview scheduling for panel and high volume hiring, integrates with Greenhouse and Lever

competitors.name: Calendly
competitors.what: General purpose booking links used by recruiters

technical_complexity.rationale: Calendar sync, interviewer load balancing and ATS integrations are standard but fiddly engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with calendars and applicant tracking systems create switching costs, but the category had established rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ATS vendors offer built-in scheduling; no acquisition of ModernLoop was found through 2026.

market_need_then: The founders cited coordinating hundreds of interviews across teams as painful at Facebook, Slack and Brex; they also cited a labor shortage in 2022 trade framing.

branding.domain_note: Began on modernloop.io; modernloop.io now redirects to modernloop.com (observed 2026, date of move not found).

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat and benefit driven: Built for recruiting heroes

brand_strength.rationale: Clear and easy name tied to the hiring loop concept, but no brand coverage, merch or community evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: ModernLoop was founded in December 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021, raised a $3.3M seed in October 2021 and a $9M Series A led by Accel in August 2022, with customers such as Instacart, Brex and Ramp on its site. No later round, layoffs or exit was found, and it appears active in 2026 as a small Series A stage company.
notes: Series A details come from the company's blog headline plus search summaries (the blog fetch redirected to the home page); Accel led per those summaries. Seed lead is described as Accel in one summary and listed as 3.1M to 3.3M by trackers; amount follows TechCrunch's headline. Total raised is 12.4M on CB Insights and 15.6M on ZoomInfo; the former matches the two rounds. Competitor sources are undated 2026 buyer guides, so there is no dated competitor evidence near the batch. Outcome search found no layoffs, sale or shutdown.
